PNR Status Check & Prediction

Check current booking status, waitlist position and chart preparation

PNR Status Check & Confirmation Prediction

Every reserved Indian Railways ticket carries a 10-digit PNR number that records who is travelling, on which train, and in which class. Checking the PNR status tells you the current booking status for each passenger on that ticket — confirmed, RAC, or still waitlisted — plus coach and berth details once they have been allotted.

Trayago reads the latest status for your PNR and, where a waitlist position exists, adds a PNR confirmation probability estimate derived from historical booking and cancellation patterns. The estimate is a statistical projection to help you plan — it is not a decision by Indian Railways, and confirmation cannot be guaranteed.

How to check PNR status online

  1. Enter the 10-digit PNR number from your ticket in the field at the top of this page.
  2. Select Check Status. Trayago fetches the current train ticket status for that booking.
  3. Review the passenger-wise booking status, chart preparation state, and the confirmation probability estimate where one is available.

No account and no IRCTC login is needed, and checking railway PNR status on Trayago is free.

Understanding CNF, RAC and WL

  • CNF — Confirmed. A berth or seat is reserved for the passenger. Coach and berth numbers appear once the reservation chart is prepared.
  • RAC — Reservation Against Cancellation. The passenger may board and is allotted a shared side berth. RAC can move to confirmed if berths free up.
  • WL — Waitlist. No berth is allotted yet; the queue position is shown as a number, such as GNWL 12 or PQWL 5. A ticket still on the waitlist after the final chart is generally not valid for travel in a reserved coach.

Chart preparation usually happens a few hours before departure and is the point at which berth allocation is finalised. Status movement is far more likely before the chart is prepared than after it.

How PNR confirmation prediction works

Trayago's PNR prediction compares your current waitlist position against how similar bookings have behaved historically on the same train, class, quota, and route, factoring in travel date and seasonal demand. The output is a probability band rather than a yes or no answer.

Treat it as guidance with real limits: unusual demand, group cancellations, quota changes, or last-minute operational decisions can all push the actual outcome away from the estimate. If the probability looks weak, it is worth exploring alternative trains or a split journey rather than waiting on the waitlist alone.

PNR status — frequently asked questions

What is PNR status?
PNR status is the current booking state of a railway ticket, identified by a 10-digit PNR number printed on the ticket or sent in the booking confirmation. It shows whether each passenger is confirmed, in RAC, or still on the waitlist, along with coach and berth details once they are allotted.
How do I check my PNR status on Trayago?
Enter your 10-digit PNR number in the field at the top of this page and select Check Status. Trayago retrieves the latest booking status for that PNR and displays passenger-wise details, chart preparation state, and a confirmation probability estimate where one can be computed. No account or login is required, and checking PNR status is free.
What does CNF mean on a PNR status?
CNF means confirmed. The passenger has a reserved berth or seat for the journey. Once the reservation chart is prepared, the coach and berth number are shown alongside the CNF status.
What does RAC mean on a PNR status?
RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation. An RAC passenger may board the train and is allotted a shared side-lower berth, typically with two passengers sharing one berth. RAC tickets can move to confirmed if berths become free before or after chart preparation.
What does WL mean on a PNR status?
WL means waitlist. The ticket has no berth allotted yet and its position in the queue is shown as a number, for example GNWL 12 or PQWL 5. Waitlisted tickets move up as other passengers cancel. A ticket that is still waitlisted after the final chart is prepared is generally not valid for travel in a reserved coach.
What is chart preparation?
Chart preparation is the point at which Indian Railways finalises berth allocation for a train, usually a few hours before departure. Trayago shows whether the chart is prepared for your PNR, because status changes are far more likely before this point than after it.
Can my PNR status change after booking?
Yes. A waitlisted or RAC ticket can move towards confirmation as other passengers cancel, and berth or coach allocation can change when the chart is prepared. Checking your PNR status again closer to departure is the reliable way to see the current position.
How does Trayago's PNR confirmation prediction work?
Trayago compares your current waitlist position against historical booking and cancellation trends for the same train, class, quota, and route, along with factors such as travel date and seasonality. The result is expressed as a confirmation probability. It is a statistical estimate, not a decision by Indian Railways, and unusual demand or last-minute changes can make the actual outcome differ.
Does Trayago guarantee confirmed tickets?
No. Trayago provides journey intelligence, status information, and probability estimates to help you plan. Only Indian Railways allots berths, and no confirmation can be guaranteed by Trayago.
Is Trayago affiliated with IRCTC?
No. Trayago is an independent travel intelligence platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by IRCTC or Indian Railways. Ticket booking is completed through official booking platforms.
